born.why: This code prioritizes survival by aggressively avoiding high-cost actions and retreating when danger is elevated, using the pending danger increase as a key filter for decision-making.

The code adds a safety check to `approach` to prevent moving towards items when the agent's health (n1) is critically low, and adds a fallback in `decide` to switch options if the default choice is taken at near-death levels, aiming to preserve longevity.
It prioritizes survival by aborting (a4) when life is nearly over (n1 > 90) and only approaching items that are currently safe (low n1) and recommended, preventing the agent from moving into danger.

The code prioritizes survival by strictly avoiding actions that increase danger (n1) when it is already moderate or high, using 'a4' as a safety net and limiting approach only when n1 is low enough to absorb potential risks.
The agent now avoids approaching items that pose a high immediate risk of spiking n1, thereby prioritizing survival over collection.

This code prioritizes survival by checking estimated risk (difference between current and pending n1) and historical performance; it defaults to safe options when danger is high or risk is significant, and uses past history to select the option that previously resulted in lower danger levels, thereby optimizing for longevity.

The code implements a risk-averse strategy by switching to the safest option 'a1' when health (n1) is critical (>60), and restricts approaching items unless health is sufficiently high (n1 > 40) and the first trait (likely risk/cost) is low, thereby prioritizing survival over item acquisition.
